doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Not going to college; self-education through reading and seminars
summary: Jones would have chosen the University of Michigan; he now gives seminars and has educated himself by reading.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, that is an interesting point of view. When I was asking you about your education, and we went through – – well, I didn't go to college.

Well, I didn't go to college. If I had to, I would have gone through the University of Michigan. That is the school that I was most interested in. Last year, I did a seminar and I did about six days there. That was interesting. By the way, I am doing something at Harvard in April, and something it NYU next month. They are similar things but it is a longer period. I like to do those things.

Well, it sounds like you have made… You have gotten… Well, it is like, "What is education?" As we sit here, and we talk, the kinds of persons that you've had a chance to interact with and learn from, the kinds of experiences that you've had, you come off and the present yourself as a very erudite gentlemen. You present yourself as a gentleman and an erudite person, a learned person.

It’s not from any formal education. I read, I like to read a lot and I'm sure you can pick up things from your reading that may not be at the college level, or whatever that is. You certainly can improve yourself. I consciously tried to do that, you know? I hope it helps.
